subject.title: [Bug]: Agents should not be able to access or modify files outside their own working space.

question: Should default host tools become workspace-contained by default, or should workspace containment remain explicit through `tools.fs.workspaceOnly`, sandboxing, or a path-policy feature?
rationale: The requested behavior changes a security boundary and an existing compatibility contract that current tests and docs still preserve, so automation should not choose the product default alone.

options.title: Default workspace containment
options.body: Make host file tools workspace-contained by default, with a documented migration/doctor path and explicit escape hatch for trusted operator workflows.

options.title: Explicit strict mode only
options.body: Keep the current default and resolve this through clearer docs plus an explicit `workspaceOnly` or path-policy configuration surface.

options.title: Defer to broader sandbox work
options.body: Treat this issue as blocked on the broader sandbox/path-policy architecture and only close it after that canonical implementation ships.

recommendation.title: Default workspace containment
recommendation.body: Make host file tools workspace-contained by default, with a documented migration/doctor path and explicit escape hatch for trusted operator workflows.

likelyOwner.reason: Their history covers both the optional workspace guard and the current unset-default behavior, making them the best available owner for the default-boundary decision.
